framework_metadata.description: Blackwell LightX2V FLUX.2 profile probe using source-built FlashAttention 2 plus FlashInfer RoPE.
framework_metadata.notes: Uses a source-built FlashAttention 2 wheel with TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST=10.0; the upstream FA3 wheel used for H200 is Hopper-only. LightX2V renamed this runner: its registry key is `flux2` (was `flux2_dev`), and the old name fails at worker init with `KeyError: 'flux2_dev'` from runner_factory -- after a full server start, so it reads as a startup failure rather than a bad name. The registry is the authority: `python -c "from lightx2v.models.runners.runner_factory import RUNNER_MODULES; print(sorted(RUNNER_MODULES))"`. The runner also requires `model_variant`: LightX2V split the old flux2_dev runner into `flux2` + model_variant dev|klein, and an absent variant fails at worker init with `ValueError: Unsupported Flux2 model_variant: None` -- a second layer behind the KeyError, each one only visible after the previous is fixed.

framework_metadata.notes: Measured on 4xB200 2026-09-14, two interleaved rounds, against the --tp-size 2 that `default` supplied on Blackwell for want of a hardware profile: 4.862 -> 4.038 and 4.873 -> 3.838, both rounds the same sign, about -19%. framework_metadata.description: Best known SGLang command for the benchmark repo default profile.
framework_metadata.notes: Keep this profile updated when the best command changes for a SGLang release or commit. Policy-aligned candidate (compile on, offload off) — NOT yet validated on H100; validate (incl. OOM risk) before publishing. FOUR-GPU CELLS ON THE 2026-09-13 4xB200 RUN ARE 3-4x SLOW AND IT IS NOT SGLANG. All three 4-GPU cases (this one, cosmos3 t2v 189f, cosmos3 i2v 189f) came out 3-4x slower than the SAME case and workload on H100 (07-03, 07-30) and H200 (08-26), three runs that agree with each other inside 2%. Every framework in those cells moved together -- sglang 0.25-0.32x, vLLM-Omni 0.28-0.30x, LightX2V 0.22x -- so the earlier note here calling it a suspected sglang regression was wrong, and is retracted. Nor is it the box: every 2-GPU case in that same run is 1.7-2.6x FASTER than its H200 figure. The discriminator is GPU COUNT, not model and not framework; the original investigation missed it because every image case is 2-GPU. Already eliminated, do not repeat: model unchanged since 2025-08-09, workload identical in both artifacts, warmup scales linearly, attention backend (`fa` is WORSE than the auto-selected dynamic_cudnn_sdpa), interconnect topology (NV18 all-pairs at 53.125 GB/s), offload off with 113 GiB free, MoE boundary 0.875 with both experts resident. SETTLED: a fresh 4xB200 does NOT reproduce it. MEASURED 2026-09-18 on a fresh 4xB200 (verda-b200-fin-03-3, same node family, sglang v0.5.20, cosmos3 t2v 189f, identical workload and the same `--attention-backend fa`): 2 GPU on cards 0,1 = 58.05s; 2 GPU on cards 2,3 = 58.24s; 4 GPU = 32.34s. Four-GPU scaling is healthy (1.80x over two), and the 4-GPU figure is 1.64x faster than H200's 53.09s -- the normal Blackwell gain. bench-0912 reported 214.90s for that same cell, 6.6x the healthy number. So the hardware is fine and these three cells are ARTIFACTS OF THAT BOX, not Blackwell and not sglang -- which is also the only account consistent with vLLM-Omni and LightX2V being equally slow there. Two further hypotheses died in the same experiment: `fa` is not pathological on Blackwell (arm A pins it and is 1.9x faster than H200), and the NUMA split that puts GPU3 on a different socket costs nothing measurable (58.05 vs 58.24 across it). RE-MEASURED 2026-09-18 and republished: cosmos3 t2v 214.9 -> 31.7, i2v 216.0 -> 31.9, wan22 669.4 -> 106.5, each now 1.68-1.98x faster than its H200 figure, in line with every 2-GPU cell. The two cosmos3 cells ran against Cosmos3-Nano e59a53c25 rather than the 7a312c868 the rest of the artifact records -- the shared cache resolves `main` online, so the revision could not be pinned; both cells reproduce under 0.1% across two runs and vLLM-Omni moved by the same factor, so the revision does not carry the result.

framework_metadata.description: Blackwell 2-GPU CFG-parallel + cuDNN-SDPA SGLang-Diffusion Cosmos3 T2I profile.
framework_metadata.notes: Measured on 4xB200 2026-09-13, two interleaved rounds. Against the previous `--tp-size 2 --attention-backend fa` command: 0.765 -> 0.576s and 0.797 -> 0.575s, about -25%, taking the cell from losing to vLLM-Omni (0.651-0.662s) to beating it. TWO changes, both measured separately. (1) CFG parallelism instead of TP: the case is guidance_scale 6.0 -- true CFG, two branches -- so one branch per GPU with the DiT replicated and one combine per step beats splitting every layer and paying an all-reduce per layer (0.765 -> 0.584, 0.797 -> 0.617). It is also what sglang's own runtime would choose: cosmos3 inherits auto_enable_cfg_parallel=True with get_auto_cfg_parallel_degree(2)->2 and _model_default_uses_cfg()->True, but `--tp-size 2` made _has_explicit_parallel_policy() true and suppressed it. The sibling Cosmos3 T2V profile already uses CFG parallel; T2I was the odd one out. (2) torch_cudnn_sdpa instead of fa, on top of that: 0.584 -> 0.576 and 0.617 -> 0.575, same sign both rounds, and far steadier -- its repeats spread 0.9% (0.572-0.577) where fa's swung 0.579-0.792. Exact softmax, same precision class as fa, and the backend vLLM-Omni serves this case with. fa2 does not run at all: there is no native transformer for it, so the loader tries a Diffusers fallback and refuses under tp>1. NOTE: at tp_size=1 that refusal no longer guards this cell -- the harness scans the server log for the fallback markers instead.

framework_metadata.description: Cosmos3 Nano T2V profile for SGLang-Diffusion main 3d540563.
framework_metadata.notes: 4-GPU CFG parallel plus Ulysses SP for long-video H200 serving; guardrails disabled, no cache. FOUR-GPU CELLS ON THE 2026-09-13 4xB200 RUN ARE 3-4x SLOW AND IT IS NOT SGLANG. All three 4-GPU cases (this one, cosmos3 t2v 189f, cosmos3 i2v 189f) came out 3-4x slower than the SAME case and workload on H100 (07-03, 07-30) and H200 (08-26), three runs that agree with each other inside 2%. Every framework in those cells moved together -- sglang 0.25-0.32x, vLLM-Omni 0.28-0.30x, LightX2V 0.22x -- so the earlier note here calling it a suspected sglang regression was wrong, and is retracted. Nor is it the box: every 2-GPU case in that same run is 1.7-2.6x FASTER than its H200 figure. The discriminator is GPU COUNT, not model and not framework; the original investigation missed it because every image case is 2-GPU. Already eliminated, do not repeat: model unchanged since 2025-08-09, workload identical in both artifacts, warmup scales linearly, attention backend (`fa` is WORSE than the auto-selected dynamic_cudnn_sdpa), interconnect topology (NV18 all-pairs at 53.125 GB/s), offload off with 113 GiB free, MoE boundary 0.875 with both experts resident. SETTLED: a fresh 4xB200 does NOT reproduce it. MEASURED 2026-09-18 on a fresh 4xB200 (verda-b200-fin-03-3, same node family, sglang v0.5.20, cosmos3 t2v 189f, identical workload and the same `--attention-backend fa`): 2 GPU on cards 0,1 = 58.05s; 2 GPU on cards 2,3 = 58.24s; 4 GPU = 32.34s. Four-GPU scaling is healthy (1.80x over two), and the 4-GPU figure is 1.64x faster than H200's 53.09s -- the normal Blackwell gain. bench-0912 reported 214.90s for that same cell, 6.6x the healthy number. So the hardware is fine and these three cells are ARTIFACTS OF THAT BOX, not Blackwell and not sglang -- which is also the only account consistent with vLLM-Omni and LightX2V being equally slow there. Two further hypotheses died in the same experiment: `fa` is not pathological on Blackwell (arm A pins it and is 1.9x faster than H200), and the NUMA split that puts GPU3 on a different socket costs nothing measurable (58.05 vs 58.24 across it). RE-MEASURED 2026-09-18 and republished: cosmos3 t2v 214.9 -> 31.7, i2v 216.0 -> 31.9, wan22 669.4 -> 106.5, each now 1.68-1.98x faster than its H200 figure, in line with every 2-GPU cell. The two cosmos3 cells ran against Cosmos3-Nano e59a53c25 rather than the 7a312c868 the rest of the artifact records -- the shared cache resolves `main` online, so the revision could not be pinned; both cells reproduce under 0.1% across two runs and vLLM-Omni moved by the same factor, so the revision does not carry the result.

framework_metadata.description: 2x B200, same recipe as enforce-eager -- the profile that actually completes a generation for this case.
framework_metadata.notes: Validated 2026-08-07 on 2xB200 (h3-b200-2gpu-v2): completes the case's T2VA request end to end -- client wall 105.76s, server-reported inference_time_s 103.06, peak_memory_mb 24546. Output verified with ffprobe directly on the returned MP4: 124 frames @ 24 fps = 5.166667s, exactly matching the requested 5s/124-frame shape (the API's own JSON `seconds` field reported a stale '4' on both the submit and completed response -- a cosmetic metadata default unrelated to the real generation params, not a real duration shortfall; confirmed by decoding the actual file). Still uses the recipe's memory-constrained --dlo-resident-layers 20 offload even though B200's 183 GB has no need for it -- vllm-omni ships only one documented 2-GPU H3 recipe, so this is that recipe as-is, not a B200-tuned command; a fully-resident vllm-omni command may be faster but is not a documented starting point. Same request, same 2xB200 hardware, sglang's b200-2gpu profile: 80.64s/80.63s client wall, 75.42s inference_time_s -- sglang is ~1.31x faster than vLLM-Omni here.

framework_metadata.description: Blackwell: the default graph with every model resident on the GPU (--gpu-only).
framework_metadata.notes: B200: --gpu-only keeps every model, text encoders included, stored and run on the card; a 183 GB B200 holds the largest graph here (MiniMax-H3: 62 GB DiT + 48 GB Qwen3-VL-32B + VAEs). Placement only, numerics unchanged. Measured 2026-09-25 on 1xB200, FLUX.1 eager, interleaved arms: default 5.94 / 5.77 / 5.79s against --gpu-only 5.56s and --gpu-only --disable-dynamic-vram 5.57s (Qwen-Image-2.1: 3.75 / 3.91 against 3.47 / 3.48) -- every --gpu-only arm below every default arm; disabling dynamic VRAM on top adds nothing, so the simpler flag is kept.
